name: Tibialis Raise
cues: Lean your back against a wall with your heels out in front of you
Keep your legs straight and your heels planted
Pull your toes up toward your shins as high as you can
Lower slowly without letting your feet slap the floor

qa.note: Family review 2026-10-01 rated minor. review: Back on the wall, knees at 3 deg. The ankle goes from -13.5 deg (feet flat under the 15 deg lean) to +19 (about normal active dorsiflexion), and the toe lift is plain in the side sheet. For the owner: the lift is modest from the -68/0.18 hero camera, the wall top is clipped, and the range is my own judgment because the research has no tibialis numbers. | skeptic: Heels stay planted (heel y 0-4 mm), knees 3 deg, the back rests on the wall, ankle -13.5 to +19, the ball rises 87 mm at the top, and the tempo is right (toe lift quick, lowering slow).
